text:
maria: Heads up — staging started hitting OOMs during a medium-traffic perf run. Pattern looks like: many short requests (seq len ~32) + large KV prefill on the same GPU.
kevin: ugh, saw a spike in workspace fragmentation in the profiler too?
maria: yes. Allocator churn goes up after the recent kernel-selector change. fragmentation_growth metric spikes right after the new kernel heuristics kick in.
kevin: do we have a flamegraph/snapshot? can you paste the perf trace?
maria: Attached snippet from nvprof timeline (trimmed):
```
GPU 0: allocations: 1200 -> 1180 -> 1250 (many small frees)
workspace_free_list growth: 42 -> 137 -> 190
kv_cache_prefill_buffers: 64MB -> 64MB -> 192MB (temp)
```
kevin: that matches: kernel selector picks a different matmul kernel for certain batch shapes which temporarily increases per-op temporary buffers. Those temporaries are same size as some KV slabs so freelist fragmentation spikes.
tony: sounds like a classic external fragmentation problem. Two quick mitigations: 1) per-request prefill cap (limit how much KV memory a single request can allocate) 2) reuse prefill buffers from a separate slab pool instead of the general allocator.
rachit: prefill cap will reduce hit rate for very long contexts though. Any numbers on how often requests actually need >prefill_cap?
maria: from the run: ~7% of requests requested >48MB prefill. They were spread across many users, not concentrated. So cap at 48MB would reduce tail OOMs but slightly increase decode latency for those 7%.
kevin: alternative: make temporary kernel buffers use a different memory arena (mmap-backed or pinned pool) so they don't fragment the main allocator. Cheaper in code than splitting KV paths.
tony: true, but that requires kernel runtime changes per backend. Might be more invasive. Reusing prefill buffers is lower-risk: we allocate a dedicated prefill-pool with fixed slab sizes (16/32/64MB) and return buffers to that pool.
sophie: quick perf question — will prefill pooling affect latency variance? If pools cold->warm transitions cause stalls, we could see jitter.
maria: measured cold starts in a synthetic run: first 50 prefill allocs are ~1.5ms slower, after that amortized cost is ~0.1ms. So small warmup penalty.
rachit: ok. Proposal: short-term = implement per-request prefill cap (config flag), add metric prefill_cap_hits and prefill_cap_latency_regression. Mid-term = implement dedicated prefill slab pool + reuse. Long-term = kernel allocator arenas to isolate temporaries.
kevin: agree. Also add a canary: rollout per-request cap to 20% of traffic in canary to validate user-impact.
tony: should we tune kernel selector to prefer lower-temp-buffer variants when fragmentation high? Might be dynamic fallback.
maria: good idea — we can add a heuristic: if fragmentation_growth > X and free_list_count_low, prefer kernel variant B. Implement as a soft switch in the selector (flag: selector_frag_avoid).
rachit: actionable tasks?
maria: I created a short action list: 1) kevin - add prefill_cap flag + metrics + canary gate 2) tony - prototype prefill slab pool (16/32/64MB slab sizes) 3) kevin + rachit - modify kernel selector to read fragmentation signals 4) sophie - add integration perf test to staging job that reproduces short-seq with big prefills.
kevin: starting on (1) today. will open PR and link e2e test harness.
tony: I'll mock the slab pool in-process first, then move to shared allocator if it proves stable.
sophie: I'll add the regression harness and a dashboard panel for prefill_cap_hits + fragmentation_growth.
dev-bot: perf-ci: nightly/staging run queued (job id: 46212). Will post results in #eng-runtime when done.
maria: thanks all. Let's reconvene tomorrow after initial PRs/benchmarks. :thumbsup:
